assumptions.text: NCCD is CCD ÷ Σᵢ₌₁ⁿ (⌊log₂ i⌋ + 1), the CCD of a balanced binary tree of the same size, as ArchUnit's LakosMetrics computes it; RACD is analyze's propagation cost.
An element is a package-level type or a function that is not a method; it is visible when exported. An internal package stays visible to its parent's tree, which one module mostly is.
Unlike analyze's Martin metrics, abstractness counts exported types only and an isolated package has instability 1, as ArchUnit's ComponentDependencyMetrics has it.

The import rules are compared over classes of packages every rule reads alike, at most 250,000 cells (classes inside × all classes), beyond which the report says they were not verified; isolations are left out, since what they allow depends on each package's captures.

Elementary cycles by Johnson's algorithm, starts and arcs in sorted order, at most 100 per graph and 20 imports per edge. A cycle set or slices rule that reaches the first cap is marked truncated, and evidence past the second says how many it left out; so does a fanOut finding's list of imports. Go forbids import cycles between packages, so only the type and subsystem graphs have them.

A fitness rule whose subject selectors match nothing is a finding unless optional, as ArchUnit's failOnEmptyShould defaults to true; so is a forbidden import, isolation or role whose patterns match nothing.

assumptions.text: Layer access counts imports between two layered packages, and with consideringAll also imports of in-scope packages without a layer. strictLayers reports imports that skip a layer; imports upward are analyze's layer-order findings.
assumptions.source: TODO.md, Ideas from ArchUnit: Layer Access

assumptions.text: A package belongs to the innermost onion ring that matches it, adapters tried in name order; packages in no ring are not checked.
assumptions.source: TODO.md, Ideas from ArchUnit: Layer Access

assumptions.text: A rule's unseen counts what its check cannot see through in the packages whose code it reads, by construct: a //go:linkname or a plugin import hides a dependency from every rule that reads code; reflection by name hides a call, a field access or a use; an unsafe conversion a field access or a use; cgo a call. A rule naming who alone may call, or what any package may import, reads every package.

A calls rule with tests reads the test files' calls from source, not types: only pkg.Name(…) through an import's name counts, an import whose name the file declares anywhere is skipped, a method call or a dot import is not seen, and a conversion such as time.Duration(n) reads as a call.

An invariant governs every field of its entities' types, since a model does not say which fields it reads, and the type's own package may write them. An exported field exposes it; a zero-value literal from another package, or a method returning a slice or map the type holds, is not seen.

An error guard is an if at the top of a body, with no init statement, that returns a non-nil error or panics; one in a switch or a loop is not seen, nor one that tests an error against nil, which passes a failure on. Guards are evidence on invariant-unenforced, never an enforcer.

An invariant claims an error guard whose function handles a type one of its entities matched, or is marked as an enforcer of the model. Guard coverage counts only for a model that declares an invariant, and the unclaimed count is ratcheted; a guard that checks the implementation stays unclaimed.
